language.script_notes: Malay in Latin script with English widely used; a wide range of indigenous languages (Iban, Kadazan-Dusun) spoken locally though rarely on road signage.

road_furniture.km_marker_style: Sabah federal routes carry an 'A' prefix before the route number, unlike the numeric-only codes on the peninsula. In Sarawak, electricity poles carry WHITE stickers (peninsular poles carry black), often with a distinctive 2-1 insulator configuration and a long diagonal wooden support brace.

architecture.roof_style: Traditional longhouses on stilts with long shared roofs (Iban/Bidayuh communities) alongside standard Malaysian mosque domes and terraced-house roofs in towns.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal and traditional thatch/shingle on longhouses.
architecture.wall_construction: Indigenous longhouses — long communal stilted buildings housing many families — are a distinctive Borneo signature; concrete terraced shophouses in Kuching, Kota Kinabalu and Miri; colonial-era architecture in Kuching.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Natural wood tones on longhouses; pastel terraced shophouses in towns.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Iban and Bidayuh longhouses on stilts; Kuching's Chinese shophouses and colonial waterfront; mosques and Chinese temples as on the peninsula; oil palm estate housing.

nature.vegetation: Vast stretches of dense tropical rainforest with some of the world's oldest rainforest; increasing oil palm plantation coverage replacing forest; mangroves along the coast.
nature.terrain: Sabah is very mountainous — Mount Kinabalu (4,095m) dominates and much of its coverage is on winding mountain roads; Sarawak is generally flatter and more riverine, with rivers serving as major transport routes.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid, very wet tropical rainforest climate — lush, dense and often cloud-shrouded in Sabah's mountains.

vehicles.plate_color: 'Q' prefix for Sarawak, 'S' prefix for Sabah.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: 4WD pickups more common given rougher roads; longboats on Sarawak's rivers.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed generations; coverage is notably sparser than the peninsula.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Sabah's coverage is largely on mountain roads; Sarawak's is flatter but patchier; significant gaps in the interior rainforest.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same island, shared rainforest terrain, similar oil palm plantations and stilt architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Malaysian plates split into TWO white sections vs. Indonesia's three; Malaysia's black-and-white painted guardrails and Perodua/Proton cars are strong tells.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Enclaved between Sarawak and Sabah, shared Borneo rainforest and Malay-language signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Brunei's plates and road furniture differ from Malaysia's; Brunei is a tiny, wealthy state with noticeably better-maintained infrastructure and an ornate golden-domed mosque skyline in its capital.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Borneo uses white pole stickers (Sarawak) vs. the peninsula's black, and Sabah's 'A'-prefixed route codes differ from the peninsula's numeric-only codes; Borneo is also more forested and less densely developed.
